lost_requests_root_causes: No centralized request intake — edits arrive via 5+ channels (WhatsApp, email, voice notes, Instagram DM, website forms) with no single system to capture them.
No handoff process from client communication to production board — requests stay in chat threads and never become tasks.
Team grew from 2 editors to 4 (Theo joined July, Kai joined September) but intake process was never formalized. Volume increased, requests fell through cracks.
Owner (Zaid) is the bottleneck — most client messages go to him, but he doesn't always relay edits to editors.

what_this_data_cannot_tell_us: Client satisfaction — we only see complaints, not whether silent clients are happy or quietly disengaging.
Actual profit margins — we have studio cost ($40/hr) and editor rates, but not overhead (rent, software, insurance, Zaid's time).
Why leads were lost — we know 19 leads were never replied to, but not whether they were disqualified internally or simply missed.
Whether Tallgrass relationship is sustainable — Tanya books and pays for two clients, but we don't know the agency's financial health or contract terms.
Video quality and client outcomes — data tracks production volume and revisions, but not whether videos drive results for clients (views, engagement, leads).

jobs.name: Spam lead detection
jobs.what_it_does: Binary yes/no classification of each lead as spam or real. Criteria distinguish gibberish names and bulk-mail domains from real business leads.
jobs.ground_truth: 4 known spam leads (L046, L066, L078, L084) out of 101 total.
jobs.expected_accuracy: High — spam signals are unambiguous (test@test.com, seo@rank1seo.biz, asdf/a@a.co, promo@fastfollowers.io).

jobs.name: Lead quality scoring
jobs.what_it_does: 3-level rubric (low/medium/high) rating each lead's fit for a Dallas video production studio based on business name, email professionalism, phone provided, and engagement signals.
jobs.ground_truth: Actual Won/Lost/New outcomes — 32 won, 42 lost, 27 new.
jobs.expected_accuracy: Moderate — Jev sees the lead form data but not the follow-up conversation, so some cold Lost leads that looked good on paper will score higher.

jobs.name: Message urgency triage
jobs.what_it_does: Scores each inbound message on urgency (0-2 rubric: routine/normal/urgent) and uses two Noul questions to flag churn signals and lost-request follow-ups.
jobs.ground_truth: 8 known high-urgency patterns (privacy/legal, contract cancellation, repeated requests).
jobs.expected_accuracy: High for urgency and churn detection; medium for lost-request detection since the follow-up language is subtler.

jev_integration.why_lead_triage: Lead triage has the clearest measurable ground truth (known spam, actual win/loss outcomes, identified urgent messages). Entity resolution was considered but harder to measure — the manual alias map was built from contextual clues that don't reduce to a simple accuracy metric.
